1227: Campground and horse hotel on the East Fork of the Greenbrier River at Durbin (Pocahontas County), bordering 300,000 acres of the Monongahela National Forest and open April 1 to October 31.  RV sites have 30-amp power and water, some with full hookups, some pull-through and some on the river; there are also tent sites, two cabins and a six-bedroom lodge across the road.  There are hot showers, municipal water, a dump station, a camp store, a pavilion and a playground; horses stay in stalls, never at the campsites.  The Durbin Rocket excursion train's depot is at the entrance, and there is no cell service, but the campground Wi-Fi handles email. --Claude
1256: Family-owned (since 1954) campground and water park at 8777 Manchester Ave. SW, Navarre, near Ohio's largest Amish community: level, easy-access sites for large RVs with water and 30/50-amp power or full hookups, open May 1 through the October 22 weekend.  It takes families only, with no tents and no alcohol anywhere in the park; swimming in the treated lake is included in summer.  Wi-Fi, a dump station and a honey wagon ($16-22) are available. --Claude
1265: Family camping resort at 8050 Edison Street NE, Louisville, open May 1 to October 15: 470 shaded RV and tent sites on 60 acres for weekend and seasonal camping, including 50-amp full-hookup pull-throughs.  There are a heated pool and spray park, a fishing pond, a restaurant, a camp store, a climate-controlled laundromat, RV repair, propane and a full-time activities coordinator, and trailers are for sale.  Reservations are required in advance, alcohol may not be carried around the resort, and only 37 sites are sold online. --Claude
1282: Family-run campground on 63 acres of rolling hills 5 miles north of Pioneer, on the Ohio-Michigan line and 10 minutes from I-80/90, open from the third weekend in April to the second weekend in October.  It has back-in and pull-through RV sites with water and electric or full hookups, tent sites and cabins, a swimming pond, a camp store, propane, showers and dump stations, and activities every weekend from Memorial Day through Labor Day.  The age requirement to camp is 21. --Claude
1312: Family-owned campground just outside Grover Hill, 20 minutes north of Van Wert, open April 15 to October 15: 209 sites on 84 acres, offered as seasonal or weekend lots.  Sites have water and 30- or 50-amp power but no sewer, back-in or pull-through, and there is a dump station.  There are showers, a 55,000-gallon pool, fishing in a pond, a quarry and a creek, kayak access, free putt-putt, a camp store selling pizza, subs and ice cream, Wi-Fi and live music most weekends.  No rate was posted when read on 2026-10-14, and CampLife takes bookings from January 1; only 12 sites are sold online. --Claude
1347: Park owned jointly by Daviess and Martin counties on the 622-acre West Boggs Lake, funded by user fees alone, so state park passes are not valid: 154 reservable RV and tent sites, most with 50-amp power and many with full hookups, plus 110 seasonal sites and two rental cabins.  Red Fox, on a peninsula into the lake, is the most popular section.  There are bathhouses with laundry, a beach, a camp store, Stoll's Lakeview Restaurant, putt-putt, a 9-hole golf course, disc golf and kayak rentals.  Reservations are paid in full and limited to two weeks, and the renter must be 18 or older; in winter, sites are first come, first served. --Claude
1476: Family-owned campground on 43 acres in Chautauqua County, 4 miles off I-86 at Falconer (exit 13), open April 15 to October 15 and home to a community of seasonal campers.  Back-in and pull-through RV sites have 30/50-amp power, water and gray-water hookups or full hookups; most fit rigs up to 40 ft and five up to 45 ft.  There are a camp store with propane and firewood, coin laundry, hot showers, fiber Wi-Fi, a koi pond, gem mining, a catch-and-release fishing pond, themed weekends and park-model rentals.  Only 26 nightly RV sites are sold online. --Claude
1759: Family campground (formerly Honey Bend Resort) at 3279 Honey Bend Avenue, Litchfield, minutes off I-55 at exit 60 near Route 66, open April through October.  It has back-in and pull-through RV sites with water and 30- or 50-amp power or full hookups, tent sites and cabins, a pool, a jumping pillow, four fishing ponds, pedal boats, putt-putt, a game room and playgrounds.  Drive-ins without a reservation are welcome; the campground is gated, so arrivals after 7 p.m. should call ahead. --Claude
1823: Family-owned campground on 160 acres in the Kittatinny Mountains at 23 Risdon Drive, Branchville, in the Water Gap area; it opened in 1966 and is open year-round, with over 200 sites, seasonal ones among them.  RV sites have water and 30/50-amp power but no sewer, and there is a dump station; reviewers have brought rigs up to about 40 ft.  There are tent sites, cabins, a pool, a lounge with a fireplace, a pavilion, playgrounds, a baseball field, a hockey rink and paddle boats.  Water is off at the sites from October through April, when stays are booked by phone.  As read on 2026-10-14, CampLife asks for at least 2 nights on every date, and the park's own page asks 2 on regular weekends and 3 on Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day weekends. --Claude
1977: Riverfront campground at 36 N River Rd, Elsberry, whose owner is bringing back the old Timberlake Marina: full-hookup sites down a wide gravel road, on well water.  It has no web page, only Facebook, and its rate is camper-reported: RV Life reviewers paid $35 a night in August 2025 and July 2026. --Claude
1980: City of Maryville park on Mozingo Lake: 128 RV sites, with pads of 20-50 ft, in three campgrounds: South (95 sites, full hookups or water and electric), North (20 concrete full-hookup 30/50-amp sites, with 20 more opening for reservations in 2027) and a 13-site equestrian campground.  53 sites are reservable online for up to 14 days; the rest are first come, first served.  There are private showers and bathrooms, a laundry, Wi-Fi at every site, a dump station, camp hosts and a visitors center selling food and essentials; the South campground stays open all winter, while the North and Equestrian close from November 1 to March 1. --Claude
1981: RV park on the old Swope Mansion grounds at 500 West Pacific Ave., in historic downtown Independence, half a mile from the Truman Home: concrete-pad sites with full 30/50-amp hookups, back-in or pull-through, and electric-only sites.  There are free Wi-Fi, a restroom and shower house, a coin-op laundry with a free ice machine, and a dump station. --Claude
2064: New campground at 495 S 39th St, Bethany, just off I-35, open year-round: large concrete sites with full hookups and 30/50-amp power, pull-throughs among them, and free Wi-Fi.  Its main building (showers, restrooms, laundry, a workout room) and cabins were still being built in September 2026, when reviewers checked in by phone; restaurants, gas and a laundromat are less than a mile away.  It has no web page, only Facebook, and its rate is camper-reported: RV Life reviewers paid $25 a night in July and September 2026 and $28 in October 2026. --Claude
